correctness.rationale: Exact proof: pairwise commutation iff all 2x2 minors vanish; primitive matrices factor uniquely modulo scalar units; valuation-stratified counting and explicit odd/even length simplification give the two terms. Burnside yields the orbit series, its two nonzero poles recover q,m, and commutator subgroup exponents obstruct isoclinism in the stated ring pair. Direct exact small-ring tuple enumeration corroborates the formulas but is not used to prove the all-arity theorem.

originality.rationale: The evaluated two-pole higher-commuting hierarchy for every finite commutative chain ring of length at least two, plus parameter recovery and the explicit mixed/equal-characteristic nonisoclinic equality family, is not established by the inspected general rationality theorem, its finite-field specializations, the general finite-spectrum theorem, or the published maximum-commuting-subset statement. General rationality, the field case and the existence of other B-equivalent nonisoclinic examples are fully credited to prior work. Remaining non-exhaustive-search risk is disclosed. value.rationale: Higher commuting probabilities and simultaneous conjugacy counts are independently motivated finite-group invariants. Their all-r exact spectrum over arbitrary finite commutative chain rings answers a natural extension beyond finite fields and distinguishes parameters visible to the hierarchy from ring structure it provably cannot detect, exhibiting nonisoclinic pairs in every prime and length at least two. The contribution is more than repeating a general rationality theorem or a two-element commuting-probability exercise.
